title: Empirical Verification of Theoretical Simplicity Priors in Trained Models

original_idea.quick_reasoning: Clearly addresses an AI Safety problem with a reasonably scoped approach.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Tests whether alignment training shifts simplicity biases. While important for theoretical alignment assumptions, the connection to actionable safety improvements is indirect. The simplicity prior hypothesis is foundational but hard to act on directly.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Generating training sets of varying description complexity and measuring OOD generalization is feasible. The conceptual challenge is rigorously defining and measuring 'simplicity' of a policy. Medium compute is sufficient for small models.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Two training set versions, OOD generalization testing, plus alignment fine-tuning impact. The experimental design is clean but generating appropriate training sets and measuring description complexity adds design work. Feasible in 30 hours if simplified.
